sender.en: “Bank of Ireland”, “AIB”, “PTSB” or another bank’s “fraud team”

name.en: Fake bank text about a suspicious payment, then a “fraud team” call to move your money

how.en: A text that looks like it is from your bank asks about a suspicious or declined card transaction and tells you to call a number. It can even land in the same thread as your bank’s real texts. The person who answers sounds calm and professional as part of the “fraud team”, but quickly creates urgency: you are told to make a payment, give away banking details, or move your money to a “safe account”. That account belongs to the fraudster.

text.en: A text “from your bank” asks whether you made a payment you don’t recognise.
It tells you to ring a number in the message, or a “fraud team” calls you.
The caller says your money is at risk and you must act now.
You are told to move your savings to a “safe account” or approve a payment.
PTSB ALERT: Was this you? A card payment of €689.00 to ZX MEDIA LTD is pending. If you did not authorise it, ring our Fraud Prevention Unit today on [number] quoting ref [number].

en: text from my bank about a payment i didnt make
rang the number in the bank text
bank fraud team told me to move my money
safe account to protect my savings
declined transaction text asking me to call
caller from aib security said my account is at risk
told to transfer my money to a new account by the bank
A phone number to ring inside a text about a suspicious payment.
Being told to move your money to keep it safe: your bank will never ask you to do this.
Pressure to act before you can check.
Don’t call any number in the text. Ring your bank on the number on the back of your card or on its official website.
Never move money to a “safe account” or approve a payment because a caller tells you to.
If you paid or shared details, call your bank straight away and report it to your local Garda station.
